text.p: Estonia's government on Tuesday approved a plan for the reorganisation and part-privatisation of state-owned Estonian Railways.
The book value of the company is around 500 million kroons but the market value is expected to be a lot less.
"The present state enterprise is going to be reorganised into a joint stock company," Raivo Vare, minister for roads and communications, told a news conference.
The deadline to form the joint stock company is September 1, he added.
The plan also foresees the formation of four companies to take over Estonian Railways major functions and which may be sold in the future although a decision has not been taken.

The four companies to be formed will operate electric trains in Tallinn and surrounding areas, one to operate passenger traffic outside Estonia, one to maintain engines and rolling stock and a company to take care of cargo transit to the east.
Vare said the plan would help the railway system gather around three billion kroons of vital investment, Vare said.

The state has decided to sell 100 percent of Edelaraudtee, formed earlier as a part of Estonian Railway, and which carries out passenger transport within Estonia apart from the Tallinn electric network.
Some 49 percent of shares held by the state in the German-Estonian joint stock maintenance company EVR Koehne will also be put up for sale, Vare added.
"I have been meeting with two possible candidates...from the U.S. and the U.K.," Vare said, speaking of possible investor interest.
The land under the railways will be held by the state, which is one way to keep some state control, Vare added.
